system_overview: This specification models the classic 'prisoners and switches' puzzle, originally presented on the Car Talk radio show. A group of prisoners must determine when every prisoner has visited a room containing two switches, without any communication outside the room. The prisoners agree on a strategy beforehand: they designate one prisoner as the counter, who uses one of the switches to track visits. If the counter correctly declares that all prisoners have visited, they all go free; an incorrect declaration results in execution.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a finite set of prisoners partitioned into two roles: (1) a single designated counter, and (2) all remaining non-counter prisoners. The room contains two toggle switches, labeled A and B. Switch A serves as the signaling mechanism for counting, while switch B acts as a dummy toggle that prisoners flip when they cannot meaningfully interact with switch A.
state_variables: The system tracks four pieces of state: (1) whether the first switch is in the up or down position (a boolean), (2) whether the second switch is in the up or down position (a boolean), (3) for each non-counter prisoner, how many times that prisoner has moved the first switch to the up position (a count from zero to two), and (4) the counter's running tally of how many times the counter has moved the first switch to the down position.
initial_state: The two switches may start in any position (both up, both down, or mixed -- the prisoners do not know the initial configuration). Every non-counter prisoner's signal count starts at zero. The counter's tally starts at zero.
actions: On each step, exactly one prisoner is brought into the room and must flip exactly one switch. A non-counter prisoner flips the first switch to the up position if it is currently down and the prisoner has not yet signaled twice; otherwise, the prisoner flips the second switch. The counter flips the first switch to the down position if it is currently up (incrementing the tally by one); otherwise, the counter flips the second switch. The counter declares success when the tally reaches twice the number of other prisoners.
safety_properties: If the counter declares that all prisoners have visited, then every prisoner has indeed been in the room at least once. The counter's declaration is never premature.
liveness_properties: The counter eventually reaches the required tally and declares that all prisoners have visited the room, guaranteeing eventual freedom.
model_bounds: The set of prisoners and the identity of the counter are declared as constants. For model checking, the prisoner set must be instantiated with a specific finite set (commonly 3 to 6 prisoners).
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for every prisoner's action, meaning every prisoner is brought into the room infinitely often. This models the warden's guarantee that no prisoner is permanently excluded. The reason each non-counter prisoner signals twice (rather than once) is to handle the unknown initial switch position: since the first switch might start in the up position, one phantom signal could be counted, so requiring two signals per prisoner with a threshold of twice the count of non-counter prisoners ensures correctness regardless of initial switch state.
